title: Applications of Generative AI in Healthcare: algorithmic, ethical, legal and societal considerations

bias_targets.methodology: Conceptual evaluation through literature review discussing how medical AI algorithms trained on non-diverse datasets that overrepresent certain groups lead to biased clinical outcomes and widen existing health disparities.

Qualitative assessment of the 'digital divide', analyzing how the infrastructure and cost requirements of healthcare AI predominantly benefit affluent communities and geographically accessible areas, thereby exacerbating health inequalities.

Theoretical review highlighting how non-representative test cohorts (spectrum bias) and discrepancies in imaging devices (measurement bias) cause medical imaging models to fail to generalize in real-world clinical settings.
